shot.description: A button the crew presses: an OBS scene, a camera preset, or both. Its label is doc.title.

scene.description: The OBS scene to put on air, by its name in OBS.

preset.description: The camera preset to recall, by its id in obs-ptz.

n.description: Where the button comes on the page, from 1.

cue.description: One press, from anyone's phone or the Operator: a shot to take, or a zoom step. The desk plays cues in the order they were written.

suggested.description: On a cue: the Operator suggested it from what the desk saw and heard, and why. The desk plays it only once a person takes it, which clears this.

why.description: The Operator's reason, in a few words.

aired.description: On a cue: the desk played it into OBS.

missed.description: On a cue: the desk could not play it, and why.

desk.description: What the desk, the page on the computer running OBS, sees: the scene on air and the scenes OBS has. The desk writes it again every 30 seconds; one not seen for 75 seconds is away.

seen.title: Last heard from OBS
seen.description: When the OBS desk last reported its status, as an ISO timestamp.
